entities.summary: Mari Evans was an African-American poet, writer, and dramatist associated with the Black Arts Movement. Evans received grants and awards including a lifetime achievement award from the Indianapolis Public Library Foundation. Her poetry is known for its lyrical simplicity and the directness of its themes. She also wrote nonfiction and edited Black Women Writers (1950–1980): A Critical Evaluation, an important and timely critical anthology devoted to the work of 15 writers. Evans died at the age of 97 in Indianapolis, Indiana. Mari Evans was a authors & novelists from Toledo (1923, Toledo–2017-03-10). A moderately significant entity in the historical record.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Mari Evans' poetry and nonfiction works contributed to the Black Arts Movement, providing a platform for African-American writers and shaping the literary landscape of North America. Her critical anthology Black Women Writers (1950–1980): A Critical Evaluation remains an important resource in feminist scholarship.
